records.central_bank: Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC) - agence d'Ebibeyin, Equatorial Guinea
records.people: Gregorio Nsue Ondo Obono (chef d'agence, BEAC agency at Ebibeyin)
records.summary: EcoMatin reports that the head of BEAC's own agency at Ebibeyin in Equatorial Guinea, Gregorio Nsue Ondo Obono, is suspected of being one of the organisers of a counterfeit CFA franc network operating across the Ebibeyin-Kye-Ossi border, that he has been held in Yaounde since late April 2024, and that BEAC suspended him and replaced him with an interim agency head; the page also reports that the head of the same agency's issuance department was questioned. This is Equatorial Guinea's first national-level case record: the only case previously shown in its box is the union-wide BEAC Paris office record expanded into every CEMAC member.
records.detail: The article (published 27 June 2024, updated 29 June 2024) states that complaints from economic agents at Abang-Minko'o and Kye-Ossi in Cameroon and at Ebibeyin in Equatorial Guinea led to joint Cameroonian and Equatoguinean investigations, and that several senior security officers of both countries were arrested in late April 2024 and held at the Secretariat d'Etat a la Defense in Yaounde, accused of facilitating the exchange of counterfeit notes across the border. It reports that on 7 May Teodorin Obiang Mangue wrote on X that a group including a senior army officer, the BEAC agency head and the Ebibeyin police commissioner had been arrested in Cameroon with 1.5 billion FCFA in counterfeit 10,000 FCFA notes, and that 50 million FCFA in counterfeit notes had been recovered on the Equatoguinean side. It reports that on 24 June BEAC governor Yvon Sana Bangui said the 2022 note series is very hard to counterfeit. Every date, name and figure written here is printed on the page at source_url. The page is paywalled in part, so the visible text may be incomplete. No quote field is given: the wording was read through a fetching tool rather than copy-pasted, and this project's rule is verbatim or nothing.
records.source_title: Guinee Equatoriale : l'agence BEAC d'Ebibeyin au coeur d'un scandale de faux billets (EcoMatin, 27 June 2024)

blanks.note: The route named in the assignment - a national Cour des comptes or Chambre des comptes finding on the BCEAO's national directorate - is closed by the BCEAO's own statutes for all seven WAEMU members, and this was read as a primary document rather than inferred. Statuts de la BCEAO (2010), read in full as text: Article 7 gives the Bank the privileges and immunities set out in the Protocol annexed to the UMOA Treaty on the territory of each member state; Article 107 provides that 'Les comptes de la Banque Centrale sont certifies par des cabinets de reputation internationale, dans les conditions arretees par le Conseil des Ministres de l'UMOA, sur proposition du Conseil d'Administration'; Article 108 sends the annual accounts to the UMOA Council of Ministers for approval; Articles 109 and 110 place control in an internal control framework and in the Comite d'Audit, whose composition is set by Articles 87 to 92. No article gives any national audit institution jurisdiction over the Bank or over its national directorates, and no national Cour des comptes is mentioned anywhere in the statutes. So a national-level case in a WAEMU member has to come from a national prosecution of agency staff, not from an audit report. Source: https://www.banque-france.fr/system/files/2025-03/StatutsBCEAO2010.pdf

Same finding for the six CEMAC members, from the BEAC's own statutes. Statuts de la BEAC modifies 2021, read as text: Article 6 grants the Bank the immunities and privileges of an international organisation on the territory of member states, including immunity from jurisdiction over the Bank, its property and its assets, and exemption of its property and assets from search, requisition, confiscation, expropriation, sequestration or any other form of seizure ordered by the executive, legislative or judicial power of the member states and of France; Chapter 4 (Articles 68 and 69) provides that the accounts are audited by Commissaires aux Comptes chosen by the Conseil d'Administration, with engagement letters signed after the opinion of the Comite d'Audit. No national Cour des comptes or Chambre des comptes is given any jurisdiction. Note the PDF is a scan whose text layer is imperfect, so no quote is offered from it. Source: https://www.beac.int/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Statuts-de-la-BEAC-modifies-2021.pdf

Inversion test run on Cameroon's own supreme audit institution. Chambre des Comptes de la Cour Suprieme du Cameroun, Rapport annuel 2023 (4.5 MB PDF from the institution's own drive, 172,000 characters of extracted text, grepped in full for BEAC, 'banque des etats' and 'banque centrale'): the central bank appears exactly once in the whole report, and not as an audited entity - it is listed among the draft legal texts the Chambre helped the finance ministry prepare, 'les projets de textes sur la gestion de la tresorerie de l'Etat, la convention BEAC-Tresor Public ainsi que le comite de tresorerie et de regulation budgetaire'. The report's own account of its jurisdiction and work covers the State, the collectivites territoriales decentralisees and the etablissements publics. BEAC is not an audited entity. Report page: https://chambredescomptes.cm/en/publications/read/rapport-annuel-2023 ; PDF: https://drive.chambredescomptes.cm/s/bq2MGTAQnBoNEF9

Inversion test run on Mali's supreme audit institution. Bureau du Verificateur General, Rapport annuel 2018 (5.5 MB PDF, 164,000 characters of extracted text), grepped in full for 'BCEAO' and 'Banque Centrale des Etats': zero hits. The section 'Domaines et nature des verifications effectuees' and the report's account of its audited entities name no central bank and no BCEAO national directorate. The only banks named anywhere are the World Bank as a donor. Confirms that the BVG route gives Mali nothing on this row. Source: https://base.afrique-gouvernance.net/docs/rapport_annuel_2018_bvg.pdf . The BVG's 2020 annual report at https://malizine.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/NET-Rapport_Annuel_2020-1.pdf returned HTTP 403 and was not read.

A real candidate that fails the rules. EcoMatin, 'Centrafrique : crise ouverte entre la police et la justice autour de l'affaire des faux billets' (28 August 2024) and 'CEMAC : apres la Guinee equatoriale, nouveau scandale de faux billets de banque BEAC en Republique centrafricaine' (9 August 2024), both read: three men (Moro Dasylva Sylvain, Yaya Saidou Younous, Aboubakar Abdoulaye) were arrested in Bangui on 8 August 2024 with more than 50 million FCFA in counterfeit notes said to have been printed in Douala; the Bangui prosecutor Benoit Narcisse Foukpio complained on 23 August that a police officer would not produce the seized stock, and the officer claimed it had been deposited at BEAC's national representation in CAR on the police director general's orders, which the central bank had not confirmed. Neither article says the BEAC national directorate or any of its staff in CAR are implicated. The bank appears only as a possible depositary of seized evidence, so there is no finding whose subject is the bank, its officials or its money. Refused. URLs: https://ecomatin.net/centrafrique-crise-ouverte-entre-la-police-et-la-justice-autour-de-laffaire-des-faux-billets and https://ecomatin.net/cemac-apres-la-guinee-equatoriale-nouveau-scandale-de-faux-billets-de-banque-beac-en-republique-centrafricaine

A real candidate that fails the rules, and a primary document. Cour constitutionnelle du Benin, decision DCC 25-028 of 6 February 2025 (downloaded and read in full, 9,100 characters of text): the applicant Delphin Zannouple, convicted on 25 January 2024 by the CRIET of complicity in embezzlement of public funds and sentenced to ten years and a 30 million FCFA fine in case CRIET/2019/RP/00191, opened on 5 April 2019, recounts that on 23 July 2018 a man posing as a bank director supplied him with funds and two air tickets for a fictitious mission to Ouagadougou, the second ticket in the name of 'monsieur Dodzi MISSINHOUN, qui serait un agent de la Banque Centrale des Etats de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO)'. That is the only appearance of the central bank in the decision: a man the applicant says 'would be' a BCEAO agent, named in the applicant's own account, against whom the Court finds nothing. Neither the BCEAO nor its Benin national directorate is the subject of any finding, and the man's employment by the Bank is asserted only in hedged terms by a convicted applicant. Filing it would assert central bank involvement the document does not state. Refused. Source: https://courconstitutionnelle.bj/files/decisions/DCC25-028_6_fevrier_2025.pdf

Guinea-Bissau searched for a national episode and nothing central-bank-related found. The most prominent recent Bissau money case was read and refused: SenePlus, 'Les millions mysterieux d'Embalo' (18 December 2025, citing Jeune Afrique of 17 December), on the 5 million euros in cash seized by Portuguese police at Lisbon's Figo Maduro airport from a plane carrying former first lady Dinisia Reis Embalo and Tito Gomes Fernandes. The article names no bank and no monetary authority at all - the only institutions in it are the Portuguese judicial police and tax authority - so there is nothing on this row. The audit route is closed for Guinea-Bissau by the BCEAO statutes finding above. Source: https://www.seneplus.com/article/les-millions-mysterieux-dembalo

Senegal's Cour des comptes was the best remaining audit lead and could not be opened. The target document was the Cour's 'Rapport definitif sur la situation des finances publiques, exercice 2019 au 31 mars 2024', the 2025 report on Senegal's understated debt, to be grepped for BCEAO - a plausible counterparty_only finding on the Treasury's accounts at the BCEAO. Two attempts by curl on https://courdescomptes.sn/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Rapport-definitif-sur-la-situation-des-finances-exercice-2019-au-31-mars-2024.pdf (both the percent-encoded and the raw accented form of the path) returned HTTP 404 with a 73 KB HTML body, and two WebFetch attempts, on that PDF and on the vie-publique.sn landing page https://www.vie-publique.sn/documents/11286/audit-situation-finances-publiques-2019-2024, were both refused with PROVENANCE_REQUIRED because a permission request went unanswered. So Senegal has not actually been tested on this document. Next round: get a working path to that PDF, and also try the Cour's older rapports publics, e.g. https://www.courdescomptes.sn/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Rapport-public-2009.pdf which appeared in search and was not fetched.

Budget ran out before these four audit institutions were opened. For each, one country-specific search was run and returned nothing on the central bank; no national audit document was read, so these countries have not been tested. The named next documents, all of which appeared in search results this round and were not fetched: BURKINA FASO - Cour des comptes annual public reports, reported by allafrica at https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202502210261.html (2023 report) and https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202512080336.html (2024 report), and by burkina24 at https://burkina24.com/?p=424483 ; the PDFs themselves were not located. TOGO - the Cour des comptes reorganised in 2022, described at https://www.labase-lextenso.fr/l-essentiel-droits-africains-des-affaires/2022-n4/togo-une-nouvelle-ere-pour-les-juridictions-financieres-DAA200t2 ; and a national education budget audit reported at https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202511250587.html . CONGO-BRAZZAVILLE - note that the auditors row already carries a documented negative for Congo saying no Congo-specific BEAC national directorate audit document could be found, which is consistent with the statutes finding above. GABON - searches returned only ministry-level embezzlement cases (Poste SA, tourism ministry, education ministry) with no central bank involvement.

One further BEAC-level vein was identified and deliberately not filed, because it is union-wide and a union key would colour all six member boxes. BEAC publishes per-subject control reports, several of which carry findings: 'Rapport de controle de la Salle des Marches' for 2019, 2020 and 2021, and 'Rapport special sur le controle du Compte d'Operations' for several years, all listed on beac.int. Search also surfaced two BEAC internal-governance stories - the cancellation of BEAC's senior officer recruitment examination after a two-year dispute over irregularities, and a nepotism audit ordered by the chairman of the board - at https://m.investiraucameroun.com/news/i/14852/beac-cancels-senior-officer-exam-after-two-year-battle-over-irregularities and https://fr.journalducameroun.com/nepotisme-a-la-beac-le-pca-commande-un-audit/ . None of these is attributable to a single member state, so under this project's union rule none of them can be filed. Recorded here so the next round does not spend budget rediscovering them.

checked_not_in_assignment: Cote d'Ivoire (CIV) - the 2011 BCEAO governor's resignation that is expanded into all seven WAEMU boxes is an Ivorian episode, so it was tempting to look for more in Abidjan. Not in this assignment, so not researched.

Guinea (GIN) - a search for 'detournement agence BCEAO Bissau' returned 'Guinee: l'ancien gouverneur de la Banque centrale condamne en appel pour detournement de fonds' (fr.allafrica.com/stories/202606250149.html), which is Guinea-Conakry and the BCRG, a different country and not in this assignment. Checked have_cases.json: GIN is present there, so it would have been a duplicate country in any case. Not pursued.

Cameroon's role in the Ebibeyin counterfeit network - the notes were said to be printed in Douala and the arrests were made and the detentions held in Cameroon, so a CMR record was considered. Refused: the people implicated on the Cameroonian side are security and immigration officers and microfinance institutions, not the central bank, and the only implicated central bank official runs the agency in Equatorial Guinea. CMR is in the assignment but gets no case from this episode.
leads_not_opened: NER and TCD above are EVENTS, not cases, and are filed in this file's 'events' array because the instruction was to write to this file only. They belong on the removals and pressure row. Whoever merges this round should route them there, or hand them to the events agent. Both are new to those countries: Niger's only event is the 2011 BCEAO forced resignation and Chad's only event is the 2009 BEAC dismissal, both union records expanded into members.

NER corroboration not fetched: 'Niger junta arrests, then releases, central bank official' at https://www.centralbanking.com/central-banks/governance/people/7960176/niger-junta-arrests-then-releases-central-bank-official , and 'Niger : ce qu'a dit la BCEAO apres l'arrestation de son directeur national' at https://www.afrik.com/niger-ce-qu-a-dit-la-bceao-apres-l-arrestation-de-son-directeur-national . The headline of the first implies he was released, which the filed source does not say; worth reading before the Niger event is used for anything beyond the detention itself.

GNQ follow-up: the Ebibeyin case was reported in June 2024 with the agency head in pre-trial detention. Two and a half years on there should be a charge or a judgment. Searching 'Gregorio Nsue Ondo Obono' plus 'faux billets' should find the outcome and would upgrade the GNQ record's status from 'under investigation'. Also unread: Teodorin Obiang Mangue's own post of 7 May 2024 on X, which the EcoMatin article quotes and which would be a second, non-trade-press source for the arrest.

TCD follow-up: the Chad suspension was reported in May 2021 with no official reason. Financial Afrik keeps a tag page for Idriss Ahmed Idriss (https://www.financialafrik.com/tag/idriss-ahmed-idriss/) and ecomatin reported a successor, 'Taoureko Hemwue Temwa promu directeur national de la BEAC au Tchad' (https://ecomatin.net/taoureko-hemwue-temwa-promu-directeur-national-de-la-beac-au-tchad). Reading the successor story would date the end of the suspension and might state the reason.

An untested route for all thirteen, which no round has tried: the national gazette. Mali's Journal Officiel is fully online at sgg-mali.ml and several issues came back in search (e.g. https://sgg-mali.ml/JO/2023/mali-jo-2023-16-sp.pdf). Congo's is at sgg.cg. A BCEAO or BEAC national directorate matter, or a court judgment against agency staff, may be published there when nothing else carries it.
